page: Amazon Web Services t3a.nano is an entry-level burstable instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and an AMD EPYC 7571 x86_64 processor clocked at 2.2 GHz. The configuration allocates 2 vCPUs across 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, alongside 0.5 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz (0.25 GB per vCPU). The instance provides no integrated local storage, requiring network-attached storage, and contains no GPUs. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 0 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned.

Benchmark evaluations reflect the burstable, resource-constrained nature of the host. Compute benchmarks show a stress-ng single-core score of 577.98 and a multi-core score of 589.58, both ranking in the lower performance tiers. Supported instruction sets include AVX, AES, and SHA-NI, contributing to a PassMark CPU encryption score of 1601.48. In application metrics, the instance handled 1.24 million Redis SET operations per second and delivered a static web serving throughput of 1.58 GB/sec.

The t3a.nano instance provides high cost efficiency for low-intensity applications where continuous full-core performance is unnecessary. Key operational tradeoffs include the tight 0.5 GB memory envelope, shared-core burst throttling, and the absence of bundled local storage. This profile is suited for lightweight utility workloads, including administrative bastion hosts, monitoring agents, low-traffic development environments, and periodic background scripts.
